default.$description: No 'Greed Standard-TRIAL' font file exists anywhere in this repo (checked directly, not assumed) — every component built against this token has been rendering in the browser's fallback font all along. Added a real iOS-appropriate fallback stack so that's a graceful degrade instead of an undefined one; swap in a real @font-face once the file is provided, don't remove the fallback.

display.$description: Same missing-font situation as font.family.default — see that token's description.

page.$description: The base canvas of the app; use it on the outermost screen background.

surface.$description: The default raised surface on the page; use it for cards, sheets and list containers.

input.$description: Fill for editable controls such as text fields and search bars.

floating.$description: Translucent glass fill for elements that hover above content, such as toolbars and floating action bars.

stacking.$description: Fill for a surface layered directly on top of another surface, so the stack stays readable.

inverse.$description: Light background for blocks that must invert against the dark UI, such as a high-emphasis banner.

scrim.$description: Dimming layer behind modals and sheets that mutes the content underneath.

default.$description: Fill for the single most important action in a view.

hover.$description: Primary action fill while the pointer rests on it.

active.$description: Primary action fill while it is being pressed.

on.$description: Label and icon colour placed on interactive/primary.

default.$description: Fill for supporting actions that sit beside the primary one.

hover.$description: Secondary action fill while the pointer rests on it.

active.$description: Secondary action fill while it is being pressed.

on.$description: Label and icon colour placed on interactive/secondary.

default.$description: Fill for actions that delete or otherwise cannot be undone.

hover.$description: Destructive action fill while the pointer rests on it.

active.$description: Destructive action fill while it is being pressed.

on.$description: Label and icon colour placed on interactive/destructive.

default.$description: Generic pressed overlay for tappable surfaces with no dedicated pressed fill.

inverse.$description: Pressed overlay for tappable surfaces sitting on light backgrounds.

disabled.$description: Fill for a control that is visible but not currently actionable.

primary.$description: Default reading colour for headings and body copy.

secondary.$description: Supporting copy that should sit one step below primary in emphasis.

tertiary.$description: Lowest-emphasis copy, for metadata, counters and timestamps.

disabled.$description: Copy inside a control that is not currently actionable.

inverse.$description: Copy placed on background/inverse or any other light surface.

default.$description: Inline link colour within running text.

hover.$description: Link colour while the pointer rests on it.

active.$description: Link colour while it is being pressed.

success.$description: Inline copy reporting a successful outcome.

error.$description: Inline copy reporting a failed or invalid outcome.

warning.$description: Inline copy raising a caution the user should read before continuing.

onAccent.$description: Copy placed on a bold accent fill.

default.$description: Hairline separating a surface from its neighbour; the default for dividers and card edges.

strong.$description: Higher-contrast border for elements that must read as clearly bounded.

focus.$description: Focus ring on the element currently receiving keyboard input.

error.$description: Border on a field whose input has failed validation.

success.$description: Border on a field whose input has been accepted.

selected.$description: Border marking the currently selected option in a set.

bold.$description: Saturated green fill for badges, chips and accents that must carry weight.

subtle.$description: Low-saturation green fill for tinted containers and section backgrounds.

bold.$description: Saturated coral fill for badges, chips and accents that must carry weight.

subtle.$description: Low-saturation coral fill for tinted containers and section backgrounds.

bold.$description: Saturated blue fill for badges, chips and accents that must carry weight.

subtle.$description: Low-saturation blue fill for tinted containers and section backgrounds.

bold.$description: Saturated magenta fill for badges, chips and accents that must carry weight.

subtle.$description: Low-saturation magenta fill for tinted containers and section backgrounds.

bold.$description: Saturated brand violet fill for badges, chips and accents that must carry weight.

subtle.$description: Low-saturation brand violet fill for tinted containers and section backgrounds.

onSubtle.$description: Content colour placed on accent/brand/subtle. Was violet.400 (4.09:1 against accent/brand/subtle, under the 4.5:1 AA minimum — found via an axe-core scan across XpPill, SessionHero and VerdictBadge, the three real components that use this pairing). violet.300 passes at 6.61:1 and stays visually distinct from accent/brand/bold, which is violet.500.

bold.$description: Saturated premium gold fill for badges, chips and accents that must carry weight.

subtle.$description: Low-saturation premium gold fill for tinted containers and section backgrounds.

bold.$description: High-emphasis fill for a message reporting a successful outcome.

subtle.$description: Tinted banner or inline-message fill reporting a successful outcome.

bold.$description: High-emphasis fill for a message reporting a failure the user must resolve.

subtle.$description: Tinted banner or inline-message fill reporting a failure the user must resolve.

bold.$description: High-emphasis fill for a message reporting a caution the user should read.

subtle.$description: Tinted banner or inline-message fill reporting a caution the user should read.

bold.$description: High-emphasis fill for a message reporting a neutral piece of information.

subtle.$description: Tinted banner or inline-message fill reporting a neutral piece of information.

surface.$description: Tinted fill marking the item currently highlighted or newly changed.

border.$description: Edge that pairs with highlight/surface to make the highlight legible.

display-l.$description: One-off hero moments such as score reveals, streak counts and celebration screens; never for text that can wrap.

display-m.$description: Full-screen result and milestone headings; not for use inside cards or sheets.

display-s.$description: The largest heading that still sits inside a scrolling page.

headline-s.$description: Card titles, list group headers and dialog titles.

headline-xs-bold.$description: Emphasis inside dense lists, and list-item titles.

headline-xs-regular.$description: The non-emphasised counterpart of headline-xs-bold in the same list.

headline-xxs-bold.$description: Compact list-item titles and tab labels.

body-m-regular.$description: Default running text: chat replies, explanations and card body copy.

body-s-regular.$description: Secondary running text, helper copy under inputs and dense list descriptions.

caption-m-bold.$description: Badge and chip labels, and emphasised metadata.

caption-m-regular.$description: Timestamps, counters, field hints and other metadata.

caption-s-bold.$description: The smallest legible label, for counter pips and micro-badges; never for text the user must read to proceed.

caption-s-regular.$description: Micro-metadata only; never for text the user must read to proceed.

mobile.$description: Reference viewport width for the mobile breakpoint.

tablet.$description: Reference viewport width for the tablet breakpoint.

desktop.$description: Reference viewport width for the desktop breakpoint.

mobile.$description: Multiplier applied to scalable sizes at the mobile breakpoint.

tablet.$description: Multiplier applied to scalable sizes at the tablet breakpoint.

desktop.$description: Multiplier applied to scalable sizes at the desktop breakpoint.

root-font-size.$description: Root font size that rem-based values resolve against; identical in all three breakpoints.
